nodes.name: NaRuO2 synthesis
nodes.procedure: NaRuO2 was prepared by mixing Na2CO3, Ru, and RuO2 in a molar ratio of 2:1:3, followed by heating at 900°C for 12 h under an Ar atmosphere.
nodes.source_text: first NaRuO2 was prepared by mixing Na2CO3, Ru, and RuO2 in a molar ratio of 2:1:3, followed by heating at 900°C for 12 h under an Ar atmosphere.

nodes.name: Na0.2RuO2 to protonated RuO2 conversion
nodes.procedure: The resulting powder was then reacted with 1 M Na2S2O8 for 3 days (100 mL per 1 g), washed with distilled water, and oven-dried. The obtained powder was reacted with 1 M HCl for another 3 days (100 mL per 1 g), with a daily replacement of the acidic solution. Afterward, the powder was thoroughly washed with distilled water and oven dried.

nodes.name: Exfoliation to layered RuO2 nanosheets
nodes.procedure: The resulting powder was dispersed in distilled water containing TBA·OH solution (250 mL distilled water and 1 mL 40% TBA·OH per 1 g powder) and stirred for 10 days. The obtained colloid was centrifuged at 4000 rpm for 10 min to remove unexfoliated precipitates. Owing to the negative surface charges of the exfoliated RuO2, the obtained colloidal suspension of RuO2 nanosheets was restored through protonation using a 37% concentrated HCl solution as the H+ source. The obtained precipitate was washed with distilled water and freeze-dried.

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM confirms atomically thin 2D morphology with thickness of ~0.7 nm and surface holes for aRu500.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The formation of atomically thin vacant nanosheets was confirmed using AFM. As shown in Supplementary Fig. 4, aRu500 exhibits surface holes and a markedly anisotropic 2D shape with a thickness of only ~0.7 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: STEM images (Fig. 1d) confirm highly disordered atomic arrangement for aRu200 component ions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The formation of a highly disordered ${ \mathrm { R u O } } _ { 2 }$ lattice after calcination at $2 0 0 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ was further confirmed from the STEM images (Fig. 1d).

nodes.characterization_summary: Powder XRD shows amorphization with broad signals and decreased (001) peak intensity for aRu100, aRu200, aRu300; rutile RuO2 reflections appear at aRu400, aRu500.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Powder X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis (Fig. 1b) confirmed amorphization during the reductive heat treatment process...

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms retention of atomically thin 2D nanosheet morphology; aRu400 and aRu500 show surface holes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Additionally, transmission electron microscopy (TEM) measurements confirmed the retention of the atomically thin 2D nanosheet morphology after reductive thermal treatment...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru 3p peaks shift to lower energy with increasing calcination temperature indicating decreasing Ru valence; O 1s shows intense shoulder peak at ~531-532 eV for aRu200 attributed to surface-adsorbed oxygen species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The impact of the reductive calcination process on the Ru valence state was subsequently verified using X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS)...

properties.description: TEM image showing highly ordered RuO2 structure

nodes.characterization_summary: Energy difference between peaks A and B reduced from ~3.1 eV for bulk RuO2 to ~2.4 eV for aRu100, reflecting 29% depression of crystal field splitting due to local structural disordering.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The increased local structural disorder around the Ru ions following reductive heat treatment was verified by O K-edge X-ray absorption near edge structure (XANES) measurements...

properties.description: Oxygen K-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy edge

nodes.characterization_summary: aRu200 shows significantly weaker FT peaks for Ru-O and Ru-Ru coordination shells indicating enhanced structural disorder; rutile-type features strengthen at higher temperatures.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Moreover, the Ru K-edge extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) data provided additional compelling support for the enhanced structural disorder following reductive heat treatment...

properties.description: Fourier Transform plot of EXAFS data

nodes.characterization_summary: aRu200, aRu300, aRu400 show diffusive featureless spectra confirming highly disordered structures; aRu500 exhibits rutile RuO2 phonon lines.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Additionally, heat-induced amorphization and phase transitions were confirmed using micro-Raman analysis...

nodes.characterization_summary: Field-emission SEM confirms retention of very thin 2D nanosheet morphology with house-of-cards-type stacking after heat treatment.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Despite these thermally induced structural changes, the very thin 2D nanosheet morphology with a house-of-cards-type stacking structure remained essentially unchanged after heat treatment, as evidenced by field-emission scanning electron microscopy...

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows distinct lattice fringes for aRu500 confirming crystallization of rutile RuO2 structure; no lattice fringes for aRu200 indicating disorder.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In contrast to the aRu100, aRu200, and aRu300 samples, the aRu400 and aRu500 samples exhibited surface holes... distinct lattice fringes were observed for aRu500, indicating that calcination at $5 0 0 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ induced the crystallization of the rutile ${ \sf R u O } _ { 2 }$ structure.
